title: psychology
aim: Explore attention, introversion, tactful advice and truth-telling games.
objectives: Use language of necessity, prohibition and permission
Ask for and give advice tactfully

lessons.title: Pay attention!
goals: Use necessity, prohibition and permission structures

grammar.title: Necessity, prohibition and permission
grammar.shortAr: الضرورة بـ need/must/have to، والمنع بـ not allowed/forbidden/not permitted، والإذن بـ allow أو permit مع المفعول وto.
points: Need + -ing and need to be + past participle express necessity when the subject is a thing.
Must, need to and have to express necessity when the subject is a person.
Be not allowed to, be forbidden and be not permitted express prohibition; mustn't and can't are more direct.
Allow / permit + object + infinitive with to express permission.
table: Necessity: thing + need to be done
The TV needs to be repaired.
You need to apply for a visa.
Adams wasn't allowed to leave the hotel.
The rules permit players to take a ten-minute break.
exceptions: Need + -ing has a passive meaning: The essay needs rewriting = needs to be rewritten.
Forbid and permit are formal and often passive: Photography is forbidden.

vocab.example: I got distracted while writing my essay.
I had to rewrite the whole thing.
It's impractical to avoid all distractions.
We often misunderstand instructions when distracted.
Distracted work can be substandard.
It is unknown exactly how much time is lost.
Loneliness can be an internal trigger.
Phones and social media are external triggers.
Be careful at moments of transition.

reading.summary: The article argues that distraction comes mainly from internal emotional triggers rather than technology, and suggests planning time, fixed checking times and care during transitions between tasks.

listening.summary: Word-stress practice with prefixed words such as rewrite, impractical and misunderstood.
Audio version of the article about staying focused.

video.summary: Speakers talk about things they never seem to find time to do.

speaking: Choose the three most useful anti-distraction tips and explain why they work for you.
writing: Turn full notes about Eyal's ideas into concise headings and keywords.

practice.why: Need + -ing has a passive meaning when the subject is a thing.

practice.q: She let me stay in her flat. → She ___ me to stay in her flat.
practice.why: Allow + object + infinitive with to reports permission.

practice.q: We ___ to stay out after midnight.
practice.why: Past prohibition uses were not allowed to.

lessons.title: Quiet
goals: Understand a conversation about introverts and extroverts
Use reporting verbs in a forum reply

grammar.title: Reported orders, requests and advice
grammar.shortAr: عند نقل أمر أو طلب أو نصيحة: ask/tell/order/advise + مفعول + to + فعل، مع تغير الضمائر والزمن عند الحاجة.
points: Use order / tell for orders, ask for requests and advise for advice.
The pattern is reporting verb + object + infinitive with to.
Pronouns and time references change, and verbs often move further back in the past.
Reported questions use statement word order, without do / does / did.
table: She ordered me to shut the door.
I asked him to open the door.
He advised me to change jobs.
She advised me not to work at the weekend.
She asked me if I was coming to the party.
exceptions: If a statement is still true or was said recently, the present reporting form can be kept.
Will is reported as would and can as could.

vocab.example: I suggested having just one meeting a week.
People refused to take the idea seriously.
I emphasised how much time we could save.
I threatened to stop coming to meetings.
He boasted about his achievements.
He claimed to have worked as a manager.
I questioned him about the details.
He admitted that it wasn't true.
I persuaded people to reduce the number of meetings.

reading.summary: A conversation compares introverts and extroverts through Susan Cain's book and workplace examples. Forum posts use reporting verbs to describe colleagues who boasted about achievements and later admitted the truth.

listening.summary: Miriam and Nishma discuss Quiet, introverts, team-building and a busy office.
Vocabulary bank practice with reporting verbs.
Pronunciation of consonant clusters in reporting verbs.

speaking: Do the introvert / extrovert quiz and explain your answers with examples.
writing: Write a forum reply giving your view on introverts or extroverts and reporting what someone said.

practice.q: She told me ___ back to my desk.
practice.why: Tell + object takes an infinitive with to.

practice.q: 'Can you open the door?' → I asked him ___ the door.
practice.why: Ask + object + to-infinitive reports a request.

practice.q: He ___ to have worked as a manager, but he admitted it wasn't true.
practice.why: Claim reports a statement that may not be true.
Reported questions use statement word order without did.

lessons.title: Here's my advice
goals: Ask for and give sensitive advice
Build on advice in a thread

grammar.title: Asking for and giving advice tactfully
grammar.shortAr: طلب النصيحة بـ What do you think I should do?، وتقديمها بلطف بـ might/could/perhaps وI hope you don't take this the wrong way.
points: Soften advice with I hope you don't take this the wrong way, Don't take it personally and I'm telling you this as a friend.
Use could, might, perhaps and maybe so advice sounds like a suggestion, not an order.
Useful forms: My advice would be to ..., If I were you, I'd ... and Have you thought about -ing?
Ask with What do you think I should do? or What would you do?
table: What do you think I should do?
I hope you don't take this the wrong way, but ...
It might be a good idea to get some lessons.
If I were you, I wouldn't leave university.
Have you thought about going to bed earlier?
exceptions: Get the wrong idea means misunderstand; take it personally means feel criticised.
If I were you uses were, not was, in this fixed structure.

vocab.example: We love to get involved and give advice.
They just want to get something off their chest.
Listening can take your mind off a problem.
We don't want to get it wrong.
Don't take it personally; it's general advice.
They rarely take advice from anyone.
Friends couldn't get through to him.
They don't seem to get the message.

vocab.ar: يفهم كلاماً بشكل خاطئ أو مزعج
vocab.example: I hope you don't take this the wrong way.

reading.summary: The blog explains that people often want sympathetic listening rather than solutions, but sometimes need honest advice. It also describes the fear of being wrong or sounding critical.

listening.summary: Two conversations with tactful advice about study, spending and friendships.
Pitch practice for sounding tactful when giving advice.

speaking: Role-play asking for and giving tactful advice about lateness, clothes or copied homework.
writing: Write an advice-thread post that builds on a previous suggestion and adds your own tactful advice.

practice.q: I hope you don't ___ this the wrong way.
practice.why: The fixed phrase is take this the wrong way.
My advice would be to ... is the tactful form.

practice.q: If I ___ you, I'd talk to her.
practice.why: If I were you is the fixed advice structure.

practice.q: Have you thought about ___ a budget?
practice.why: Think about is followed by the -ing form.

lessons.title: Would I lie to you?
goals: Use fillers to gain thinking time

grammar.title: Fillers and buying time in conversation
grammar.shortAr: كلمات مثل Well و So و OK و Right تمنح وقتاً للتفكير، وتعبيرات مثل Let me think تؤجل الإجابة بلباقة.
points: Fillers such as Well, So, OK and Right give the speaker time in informal speech.
Phrases like Let me think and I'm just trying to remember buy time before an answer.
They show that a response is coming; they are not complete answers.
They are useful when telling a true-or-false story in a relaxed conversation.
table: So, you already had that bag?
OK, that's interesting. / Right, so I'd taken a shirt.
Let me think. I'm just trying to remember.
That's a good question. I'll have to think about this.
exceptions: Fillers suit informal speech; avoid overusing them in formal writing.
They do not answer the question, so follow them with a real response.

vocab.example: Well, that's very interesting.
So, you already had that bag?
OK, that's interesting.
Right, so I'd taken a Brazil shirt.
Let me think before I answer.
That's a good question; give me a moment.

vocab.word: I'll have to think about this
vocab.example: I'll have to think about this before I decide.
I'm just trying to remember the year.

reading.summary: The lesson introduces Would I Lie to You?, a BBC panel show where celebrities tell stories that may be true or false. Dan Walker's story involves a Brazil bag and Pelé.

listening.summary: Olga tells her story in the BBC game while the other players ask questions.
The answer to Olga's story and the players' reactions.
Review audio for a text about burnout and ways to deal with it.

video.summary: BBC programme clip with Dan Walker's Pelé story from Would I Lie to You?

writing: Write an email giving a friend news and including a short surprising story.

practice.q: Which word is a common informal filler that buys time?
practice.why: Well is a typical filler in spontaneous speech.

practice.q: You want to delay an answer. Best phrase:
practice.why: It gives the speaker time to think.

practice.q: "That's an interesting question" is used to ...

practice.why: They help manage relaxed, spontaneous conversation.

review.summary: Review of focus and distraction, reported speech, tactful advice and conversation fillers, with a burnout text.
tasks: Choose the correct necessity and prohibition forms in descriptions of unusual jobs.
Report requests, orders and advice with ask, tell and advise.
Correct collocation mistakes and complete the burnout text with the review audio.

If I ___ you, I'd draw up a schedule.

Which verb means 'talk proudly about your achievements'?
What does Nir Eyal see as the main cause of distraction?

Polite way to give honest advice:
options: I hope you don't take this the wrong way, but ...
quiz.answer: I hope you don't take this the wrong way, but ...

quiz.q: Which phrase buys time before an answer?
Reported request from 'Can you carry my suitcase?'
options: She asked me carry her suitcase.
She asked me to carry her suitcase.
She asked me carrying her suitcase.
quiz.answer: She asked me to carry her suitcase.
